item.text: IBAC reported on corruption in Victorian prisons through four investigations: Operations Rous, Caparra, Nisidia and Molara.
item.support: This report focuses on four investigations – Operations Rous, Caparra, Nisidia and Molara

item.text: It examined conduct in public and private prisons, including assaults, information misuse, undisclosed associations and tobacco smuggling.
item.support: including excessive use of force, masking behaviours, misuse of information, inappropriate relationships and trafficking of contraband

item.text: IBAC found excessive force and failures in incident reporting at Port Phillip Prison, and identified improper relationships, information access and payments for tobacco smuggling in other investigations.
item.support: IBAC found corrections staff at Loddon and Dhurringile Prisons corruptly received cash payments to smuggle tobacco

item.text: It made three additional recommendations on prison controls and training, a statutory duty to report suspected corruption and a culture that supports reporting.
item.support: introduce a statutory obligation on corrections officers to report to the prison governor or to IBAC

item.quote: In Operation Rous, IBAC found that certain corrections officers at Port Phillip Prison had used excessive force against two prisoners, one of whom has an intellectual disability.
In Operations Nisidia and Molara, IBAC found corrections staff at Loddon and Dhurringile Prisons corruptly received cash payments to smuggle tobacco into the facilities.

item.heading: Summary of investigations and key findings
